title: Trace-triggered conditional alert fencing and anomaly scorer for SLO incidents
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current SLO alerting pipeline treats metric-derived burn-rate triggers and trace/log anomalies as independent signals. This causes noisy pages for transient tail-latency spikes and poor actionability when a downstream kernel regression manifests as increased error-rate in specific trace paths.

Goal: Build a combined flow that: (1) accepts trace-derived signals (span-level error / latency signatures) to gate and fence burn-rate alerts, (2) computes an anomaly score per SLO using fused signals (metrics, span patterns, log signatures), and (3) applies hierarchical paging attenuation so only high-confidence incidents escalate to on-call. The feature should be pluggable into both Hosted and Dedicated runtimes and maintain existing SLO dashboards.

Scope:
- Trace hook enrichment: lightweight span classifiers that tag spans with anomaly markers during ingestion.
- Anomaly scorer: small service that consumes metrics, traces, logs and emits a normalized score (0-100) per SLO window.
- Alert fencing: conditional rules that can (a) mute burn-rate alerts when trace score is low, (b) escalate to pager only when score + burn-rate > threshold, and (c) generate advisory slack messages otherwise.
- Dashboard updates and runbook hints: surface trace anchors, top contributing spans, and suggested mitigations in the SLO incident panel.

Non-goals: rewriting metric ingestion or replacing existing burn-rate logic completely. This is an augmentation layer that can be toggled per-customer or per-SLO.
acceptance_criteria: Score service emits anomaly_score metric for each SLO window (1m/5m/15m) and is queryable from Console
Burn-rate alert policy can reference anomaly_score and supports conditional fencing expressions
Pages reduced by >=45% for known flaky transient tail-latency regressions in internal prod during gated rollout (canary on 2 services)
Dashboard incident view surfaces top 5 trace anchors and links to trace explorer for immediate triage
Integration tests for trace hooks, scorer, and alert policy evaluation added to observability CI
Feature flag + rollout plan exists and can be disabled per-customer
implementation_notes: Trace hooks will run as a filter in the span-ingest pipeline (sidecar-instrument-friendly); initial classifier is a ruleset combining latency percentile heuristics with span error codes
Anomaly scorer is a lightweight aggregator (Go) exposing Prometheus metrics; uses exponential smoothing over burn-rate and a small logistic map to combine signals
Alert fencing implemented in policy-evaluator service; add expression language support: e.g., (burn_rate > 4) && (anomaly_score > 60)
We must ensure scorer adds <2ms p95 overhead to ingestion path — run performance microbenchmarks on canary cluster
Telemetry: emit explainability tags (which spans contributed) to incident trace bundle for postmortems
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed. Validated span-level rule heuristics on 72h of prod traces; identified three high-signal span patterns for model phase-out.
2026-03-03: Prototype anomaly scorer service implemented; exposes anomaly_score and contributing_signatures metrics. Local load test shows 2000 sps with <1ms median processing.
2026-03-04: Policy-evaluator PR opened (github.com/redwood/observability/pulls/789). Initial expression syntax reviewed by runtime team.
2026-03-05: Canaries planned: two Redwood internal services (ingest-parser, tokenizer-runtime). Feature flag gating and per-customer toggle implemented in Console backend.
review_feedback: PM (Lina Gomez): Prefer conservative default thresholds and an opt-in rollout for external tenants to avoid surprise pages.
Design (Evan Lee): Incident panel mockups look good; request to include explicit 'Why muted' banner when an alert is fenced.
Security (J. Morales): Need data-flow diagram showing span attributes retained and PII stripping applied before scoring — security review required before canary.
SRE (Olivia Chen): Suggest adding an automatic fallback that re-enables burn-rate pages if scorer becomes unavailable.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False negatives (muting real incidents) — Mitigation: conservative thresholds and automatic fallback to full burn-rate if scorer health degrades
Risk: Performance regression in span ingestion — Mitigation: implement scorer as async consumer and keep hook cost minimal; do perf budgets and litmus tests
Risk: Alert policy complexity causing operator confusion — Mitigation: ship templated policy presets (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and clear Console UX
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal canary): enable on ingest-parser and tokenizer-runtime with verbose logging and PagerDuty only for P1 incidents
Phase 1 (beta customers): invite 3 customers on Dedicated with opt-in; collect paging and signal metrics for two weeks
Phase 2 (wide): make feature available in Console with default disabled; provide migration doc and one-click presets
Safety: automatic disable if scorer error rate >1% or latency >50ms sustained for 5m
